spec.title: High inlier scene
spec.input: frame pairs with a measured baseline over 15 px on a texture-rich scene
spec.expected: a large, consistent inlier set that satisfies v3 §14’s usable figures
spec.passCriteria: >= 15 judged frames; median inliers >= 30 and median inlier ratio >= 0.35 (both v3 §14); the inlier set’s spatial spread clears 20 px; RANSAC reached its own confidence target rather than its cap
spec.failureCondition: a ratio that clears the bar on a set too small or too clustered to determine a model; or a run where the iteration cap always bound, so the reported ratio is whatever the last sample gave rather than an estimate with a probability behind it

testResults.observed: 406 judged frames: median 147 inliers of 147 correspondences (ratio 1), baseline 38.94 px, spread 122.84 px; 0 frame(s) hit the iteration cap
testResults.reason: a consistent subset of the tracked correspondences agrees on one geometric model, at v3 §14’s usable figures. On its own this proves nothing — a verifier that accepted everything would report a ratio of exactly 1.00 — and GEO-003 is what separates the two

spec.title: Low texture scene
spec.input: frames the worker classified TEXTURE_POOR, where few correspondences exist
spec.expected: the phase declines to verify, and says so
spec.passCriteria: >= 15 texture-poor frames; every frame with fewer than 20 correspondences or fewer than 30 inliers reports UNVERIFIED — never USABLE, never GOOD; the state never disagrees with its own inputs
spec.failureCondition: a USABLE or GOOD verdict reached on a correspondence set too small for v3 §14’s minimum

testResults.observed: 125 texture-poor frames, 0 judgeable: median 0 correspondences, -1 inliers; 125 UNVERIFIED, 0 USABLE, 0 GOOD
testResults.reason: where the scene did not supply enough correspondences, the phase reported that rather than a ratio computed over four points. §44’s fail-closed rule says the same thing: when the information is not there, lower the state rather than making the result convenient

spec.title: Outlier-heavy scene
spec.input: the real correspondence set with 30% of its targets displaced 25 px by the harness, handed to the verifier unmarked
spec.expected: RANSACでOutlierが除外される — v3 §66’s pass condition, verbatim
spec.passCriteria: >= 10 injected frames; >= 0.9 of the injected outliers rejected; <= 0.3 of untouched correspondences rejected; the surviving inlier count still reaching 30; and the injected rejection rate at least 3x the untouched rate
spec.failureCondition: injected outliers accepted as inliers. A verifier that returns everything scores a recall of 0.00 here while satisfying every criterion in GEO-001

testResults.observed: 68 injected frames: 100% of the injected outliers rejected against 0% of untouched ones, 91.5 inliers surviving
testResults.reason: the verifier found outliers it was never told about. The harness displaced 30% of the targets by 25 px and handed the set over unmarked; this is the one number in Phase 5 that a stage returning its input cannot produce, because returning its input scores exactly 0 while satisfying every count-based criterion v3 §14 names

spec.title: Planar scene handling
spec.input: every judged frame — both a fundamental matrix and a homography are fitted on all of them
spec.expected: v3 §16’s comparison is made, and PLANAR SCENE follows from the two inlier counts
spec.passCriteria: both models fitted on >= 15 frames; the planar flag follows from the two counts on every frame; both counts recorded per frame; and both outcomes seen, or the run reports which it never saw
spec.failureCondition: a run that fitted only one model; or a PLANAR flag that does not follow from the two counts beside it

testResults.observed: 495 frames with both models fitted: 418 planar, 77 non-planar; median 152.5 fundamental inliers against 111 homography
testResults.reason: both models were fitted on every judged frame and the planar flag follows from their two counts. The fundamental matrix is the weaker constraint and normally admits at least as many points, so the homography reaching it is the signal — and v3 §16 requires that case to lower translation confidence in Phase 6, because an Essential matrix decomposed from a planar scene is degenerate and gives a pose that looks entirely reasonable

spec.title: Verification cost
spec.input: the measured cost of the RANSAC pass per frame
spec.expected: verification fits §H’s budget, with the correspondence count recorded alongside
spec.failureCondition: over budget. Advisory because §34 ranks correctness above performance, and because a device budget cannot be adjudicated off the device (§H.4)

testResults.observed: 0.562 ms mean over 400 frames at a median of 147 correspondences, both models fitted, 0 frame(s) at the iteration cap
testResults.reason: verification fits its budget with both models fitted on every judged frame

spec.title: Metadata honesty
spec.expected: the phase claims a model only where it verified one, and no term it cannot measure
spec.passCriteria: inliers plus outliers equal the correspondence count on every frame; no frame reporting UNVERIFIED carries a model; the state is never inconsistent with its own inputs
spec.failureCondition: any of the above unmet — in particular a model attached to a verdict of none

testResults.observed: 620 frames inspected: partition intact, no model on an unverified frame, no state inconsistent with its inputs, 125 frame(s) reported as degenerate rather than verified
testResults.reason: the record says what was verified and nothing else. §15’s reprojection error stays null through this phase: an inlier’s residual against a fundamental matrix is a Sampson distance, not a reprojection error, and calling it one would be claiming a pose that has not been computed

controller.note: Every decision carries the median worker latency and the budget it was compared against. The controller reads no clock of its own — only the timestamps on the samples it is given (§59).

segmentLog.note: The timeline is cut wherever load injection was switched on or off. FRAME-001 reads the longest unstressed segment; stressed segments are measured and reported but never counted toward continuity.

crossCheckDetail.note: Each pair is one video frame measured twice: on the main thread with an independent 64x48 readback, and in the worker on the pixels the pipeline actually delivered. The readback costs what §H.1 measured, which is why it runs at 1 Hz and is excluded from the pipeline UI cost in FRAME-005.

pipeline.note: Frames declined by rate pacing (pacedOut) are the scheduler working as designed and are not drops. Frames declined because the worker was busy (backpressured) are deliberate too. Only `lost` counts frames that were handed over and never came back, and only that is held against FRAME-001.

refill.note: What §11's refill produced each frame and why each point was or was not admitted. Declined-too-close means the point is already being tracked, which is a healthy tracker rather than a failing one; declined-out-of-reach means it sat where the solver's window cannot cover it. Without the split, a population below §11's minimum cannot be told apart from a detector that found little.

flow.note: Motion classes are measured from the image by an integer SAD translation search on the pyramid’s top level, which shares no code with the Lucas-Kanade solver and never reads the feature list. `tracked` counts only points carried forward from the previous frame; `redetected` counts what §11’s refill added, and the two are never summed into a survival figure — a refill can top the population back up while the tracker is losing everything.

current.reason: 135 inliers at ratio 0.931 — both of v3 §14's GOOD conditions met

injectedOutliers.note: GEO-003. The harness displaces a known fraction of the correspondences by a known amount and hands the verifier the set with no marking. `medianRecall` is the fraction of the harness’s own outliers the verifier rejected — the one number in this phase a stage that returns its input cannot produce, because returning its input scores exactly 0 while satisfying every count-based criterion v3 §14 names.

planarHandling.note: v3 §16. Both models are fitted on every judged frame, never skipped as an optimisation: the fundamental matrix is the weaker constraint and normally admits at least as many points, so the homography reaching it is the signal that the scene is planar. Phase 6 lowers translation confidence there, because an Essential matrix decomposed from a planar scene is degenerate and yields a pose that looks entirely reasonable.

overlayAlignment.note: Carried into Phase 5 from Phase 3 for the same reason, and it binds harder here: a correspondence is two positions in the acquired buffer's frame, so a buffer rotated against the video makes every baseline and every residual in this bundle a measurement of the wrong thing, while every count-based criterion v3 §14 names still passes (§H.7).
